UPDATE: Hope and Healing

By: Laura Byrne | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A doctor changing lives by changing faces - and now extending her philanthropic reach.

Unique Selling Point:
Dr Ansua Steyn is an aesthetic surgeon who, last year, realized that there is a great need for a foundation to help those in dire need of facial reconstructive surgery. She collaborated with a team of experts to start offering surgery pro bono to those who cannot afford it. Now her reach is extending through partnerships with state and private institutions, and this month she will collaborate on a project to provide a corneal replacement and restore a man's sight.

Script:


UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: I’m a doctor, and I love helping people.
VOICEOVER: In March this year, we brought you the story of an aesthetic surgeon on a quest.
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: I’m going to try and change the world, one patient at a time.
UPSOUND: CB ARCHIVE: Claire: Hello hello Melvin!
Melvin: Hi Claire, how are you?
VOICEOVER: Dr Ansua Steyn and her team transformed life for Melvin Maxim, struggling with large keloid scars…
UPSOUND: CB ARCHIVE: Lelitha: Ready or not, here I come!
…and eight year-old Lelitha Jantjies, traumatised by a vicious dog attack.
Can we show you how you look? Okay, let’s look!
Lelitha: Wow!
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: even though it’s a work in progress, she feels beautiful. And you can see it in her eyes.
UPSOUND: CB ARCHIVE: Dr Ansua: Hello my liefietjie! Hoe gaan dit?
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: Since the interview with Carte Blanche, so many things has happened. We are getting emails, phone calls daily. I never knew that there was such a need specifically in our community, never mind in South Africa.
UPSOUND: Hello julle! Welkom, welkom!
VOICEOVER: One call came from Gerhard Botha.
UPSOUND: GERHARD BOTHA: I can see figures. The lighter it is, the harder it is for me to see.
The lighter, the harder?
Yes.
VOICEOVER: Blind in one eye from birth, he recently lost sight in the other due to an infection.
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: He lives in our community. He is 37 years old and he cannot see. And I knew we had to help him.
UPSOUND: GERHARD BOTHA: If I focus it feels like I can see a V and an N.
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: And then I realized I knew who to call.
UPSOUND: GIFT OF SIGHT (YOUTUBE): I’m Dr Johan Kruger…
UPSOUND: JUANDRE KRUGER: The Gift of Sight was founded to help people in need who don't have access to private healthcare, to reduce the backlogs in cataract surgeries.
VOICEOVER: Dr Ansua joined hands with eye surgeon Dr Johan Kruger and his son, former Springbok rugby player, Juandré Kruger.
UPSOUND: DR JOHAN KRUGER: There’s, in fact, over 100,000 blind people in this country that need help.
UPSOUND: JUANDRE KRUGER: Life is full of special moments. And imagine not being able to experience those moments, with your loved ones, and to experience this wonderful country. So, you know, everyone has a right to sight.
UPSOUND: THERESA BOTHA: You’ve got this!
VOICEOVER: This month, Gerhard arrived at Dr Kruger’s Cape Town surgery for a life-changing laser cornea transplant.
UPSOUND: DR JOHAN KRUGER: He's not able to work or to drive anymore. And I'm going to do a corneal graft on this patient…
VOICEOVER: Both foundations contributed funds towards the considerable expense of buying a donated cornea. The cornea is the eye’s outer lens, protecting it from dust and UV rays, and focusing most of the light that enters the eye.
UPSOUND: Ansua: Don’t let it fall!
Dr Kruger: The important thing is not to drop it on the floor.
UPSOUND: GERHARD BOTHA: I'm feeling excited. A little bit stressed, which I think is normal, but I also feel very blessed.
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: So the cornea transplant was the first time I've seen this in my whole life. And I must say, it was absolutely incredible to witness.
VOICEOVER: After the cornea was cut to size, a steady hand was needed to place it.
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: And then the little sutures that had to be done through a microscope because they were so, so small. It was it was actually a piece of art.
VOICEOVER: Gerhard is recovering well…he’ll need extensive follow-up for the next year. But Dr Ansua has also been extending her impact closer to home, in a collaboration with the George Provincial Hospital.
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: So what we do is I come in with our team, we do a reconstructive case, and then we stay and help them with their overflow of surgical patients.
UPSOUND: MEC WENGER: What this partnership means is that patients who have more complicated cases or rarer conditions who would otherwise have to travel all the way to Cape Town to receive care can now receive this care closer to home.
VOICEOVER: Mireille Wenger is the Western Cape MEC for Health and Wellness.
UPSOUND: MEC WENGER: It’s through partnerships like this that we can really increase access to care.
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: We can now help more than one person a month. I think currently we're standing at 4 or 5 per month.
VOICEOVER: Despite surpassing her goal, Dr Ansua is not slowing down.
UPSOUND: DR ANSUA STEYN: I have a waiting list of about 20 patients that I want to help, but I can't help all of them all at once. So I want to challenge everyone. You don't have to be a doctor. Let's just all try to help one person per month. We can really just make a difference in this country.
